prompt:
I need the front end for Paperlark. A consumer site for designing and ordering printed invitations, announcements and envelopes, used by millions of people for weddings, birthdays and showers who type in their event details and guest addresses for printing.

Who's using it: Hannah Liu, 31, an ICU nurse planning her wedding in Sacramento on her days off. She's never ordered printed stationery before and is doing this on her laptop after a 12-hour shift; her fiancé, Marcus, collected half the addresses in a spreadsheet and she collected the rest from texts.

What they're doing right now: Hannah picked an invitation design last week and is now filling in everything that will actually be printed: the couple's names as they should appear, the ceremony and reception details, the RSVP deadline, and the recipient names and addresses for 92 envelopes. She just pasted in Marcus's spreadsheet, and the site flagged problems: some addresses it couldn't verify, a few duplicates, names in the wrong column, and one RSVP date that falls after the wedding. She needs to fix these before the proof is generated and the order goes to print, since printed items can't be corrected later.

What's in the system at this point: Order #PL-4471-9083: 'Garden Arch' wedding invitation, 92 invitations + 92 RSVP cards + 92 return-addressed envelopes with guest addressing. Event fields: names ('Hannah Mei Liu & Marcus James Reyes'), host line ('together with their families'), date Saturday, May 15, 2027, ceremony 4:00 PM at 'St. Francis of Assisi Church, 1066 26th St, Sacramento, CA 95816', reception 6:00 PM at 'The Firehouse Pavilion', RSVP-by date (currently entered as 'June 1, 2027', invalid), wedding website URL. Guest addresses: 92 entries (51 from Marcus's import, 41 typed). Issues found: 6 addresses unverified (e.g., missing apartment number, ZIP 95818 vs city 'Davis'), 3 likely duplicates ('Aunt Rose & Uncle Ben' and 'Rose and Benjamin Tan'), 4 entries with first/last name swapped, 2 international addresses (Manila, Vancouver BC) needing country format, 1 entry with an emoji in the name line. Character limits: names 40, address line 45. Print cutoff for guaranteed delivery by Feb 1: order by Dec 4.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
